title: M. microti as a vole-associated MTBC name
dek: A Wikipedia wildlife ecotype. Rare in human pulmonary queues. Still able to confuse an MTBC NAAT if you never look at the tree.
story: M. microti is Wikipedia's vole-associated MTBC member. Human disease exists and is uncommon. The value of the page is to keep wildlife ecotypes on the roster so a weird tree is not auto-classified as contamination.
Historically it was used as a vaccine candidate in some countries; that history is not a modern TPT regimen.
Like other animal-adapted leaves, NAATs may light. Speciation is WGS or a dedicated barcode, not a cartridge brand.
deep: Do not spend the Wikipedia article inventing a vole-to-human transmission model for every case. Ask epidemiology after the name is known.
Vaccine-history trivia is not WHO TPT.
Microti can look 'not H37Rv enough' to a fussy mapper. Same hygiene as canettii, different taxon.
Related wildlife names (mungi, suricattae) may not even have stable Wikipedia pages; WGS literature still names them.
